title: The Sita who wasn't there
hookLine: Indrajit cuts Sita down in front of the army, or seems to: it's maya
carry: maya makes the false look real; look again
last: MANY TELLINGS, ONE RAMA, KEPT ALIVE BY RECITING.

cards: Indrajit rides out of Lanka's western gate with a woman in his chariot. She's thin, in a soiled garment, weeping, calling Rama's name. Hanuman sees her and freezes.
He sat in the tree above her in the ashoka grove; he knows that face. It's Sita. In front of the whole monkey army, Indrajit seizes her by the hair, draws his sword, and cuts her down.
Then he shouts across the field: there's nothing left to fight for now.

teach.b: Hanuman, who crossed the sea to find her, pulls the army back in despair and goes to tell Rama. Rama, hearing it, collapses.
Then Vibhishana arrives, the one person in the camp who knows how Lanka thinks. That wasn't Sita, he says. Ravana would never allow her to be killed; he wants her too much.
It was an illusion, a magic double, and a distraction. Right now Indrajit is at Nikumbhila, a sacred grove and shrine, to complete a fire offering. If he finishes it, he'll be unbeatable.
But Brahma's boon has a condition: whoever attacks him there, before the rite is done, can kill him.

teach.h: MAYA: WHAT APPEARS, NOT WHAT IS.
teach.b: Tellers call that false woman maya-sita, the illusion Sita. And maya is one of Hinduism's big words.
It means a power that makes things appear, and in Vedanta, one school of Hindu philosophy, it names the way the world can look like the whole truth when it isn't.

teach.h: IT ONLY NEEDS TO GRIP THE HEART.
teach.b: Many teachers use this scene to show how maya works on us: it doesn't need to be real; it only needs to grip the heart.

teach.h: MAYA MAKES THE FALSE LOOK REAL. LOOK AGAIN.
teach.b: The tradition's answer has a name too: viveka, discernment, telling the real from the seeming. Notice that Vibhishana isn't stronger than anyone. He looks again, with a calm mind, and knows.
Rama, steadied, sends Lakshmana off with Vibhishana, Hanuman and an army. The race to Nikumbhila begins.

how: Some Ramayana tellers use the illusory Sita, the māyā-sītā of this episode, to talk about māyā, illusion, and how fear can make what is false look real.

o: the night Indrajit is captured and made to serve Rama
the end of Ravana's son, which begins with a magic Sita
Indrajit's escape from Lanka after his father's fall

games.q: maya and viveka — tap the pairs.
p: a power that makes things appear
telling the real from the seeming

s: it was an illusion, a magic double, meant to stop the army.
maya is only a word for a magician's trick
it's also a big Hindu word for how what appears can pass for the whole truth.
it is Vibhishana, not Rama, who sees through the trick
Rama collapses in grief; Vibhishana looks again with a calm mind and explains it.

games.q: a scary screenshot lands in your group chat and everyone's already panicking. what's the viveka move?
o: ask what you actually know before you react, like Vibhishana.
decide nothing's real, so none of it matters.
games.why: viveka isn't believing nothing. it's looking again: Vibhishana knew Ravana, so he could tell the real Sita from the maya.

practice: Picture a fear your mind has been showing you lately, a scene of something going wrong. Breathe slowly.

If you pray, say Rama's name softly on each breath, the way many Hindus steady the mind with a name of God; if you don't, just say: look again. Then ask, in Vibhishana's calm voice, what you actually know.

wordCard.voice: Indrajit's death. It begins with his cruelest trick, a magic Sita cut down before the army, and Vibhishana seeing through it to the fire at Nikumbhila.

orig.note: Sanskrit māyā: magic power or illusion; Indrajit's double of Sita is called māyā-sītā, the illusory Sita.

carryVoice: Your line: maya makes the false look real; look again. The race reaches the grove next. Day six hundred fifty-two.
